rows.selection_reason: No prior experiments exist, so the first step is to establish a baseline. This experiment tests the simplest configuration (RNA-only, single-profile, PCA encoder) to understand if RNA data alone can achieve reasonable performance. It isolates the effect of the RNA encoder and profile setting, providing foundational evidence for comparing more complex models later.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with PCA encoding achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It directly addresses whether multiprofile improves performance and how avgpool compares to no aggregation, providing critical insights with minimal additional complexity.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile (config_002, 0.590 accuracy) outperforms singleprofile (config_001, 0.485). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 (config_002) to scvi_n200 while keeping multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (same as config_002) improves accuracy. This isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, without changing multiple variables. It balances exploration (testing a new encoder) and exploitation (building on the multiprofile advantage).

Existing evidence shows that rna_only models with multiprofile and scvi_n200 encoder (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (used in config_005) with transformer aggregation improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It builds on the promising direction of scvi_n200 and multiprofile while exploring a key design choice with minimal additional complexity.

Existing evidence shows that for RNA-only multiprofile settings, transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool (config_006 vs config_005). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt (a more advanced model) while retaining transformer aggregation (a promising choice) improves performance. It isolates the effect of the RNA encoder, a critical design choice, and builds on the strong evidence for transformer aggregation.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation achieve the highest accuracy (0.6529). This experiment tests whether adding image data (resnet50) to this strong RNA-only base improves performance, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It directly extends the best RNA-only configuration to explore multimodal benefits, balancing exploitation of proven RNA settings with exploration of image data integration.

Existing evidence shows that config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (a more modern architecture) improves performance while keeping other parameters fixed. This isolates the impact of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision, and helps determine if the current best model's image encoder is optimal.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (config_033) achieve the highest accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether using the imagenet_vit_l image encoder (a stronger baseline) with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (instead of transformer aggregation and weighted fusion) could improve performance. It isolates the effect of image encoder choice and aggregation method, which are critical design decisions with uncertain impact. This is a logical extension of the current best configuration and helps validate whether the current success is due to specific components or general multimodal synergy.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l achieve high accuracy (config_036: 0.715). This experiment tests whether changing fusion from concat to weighted (while keeping avgpool aggregation) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It builds on the strong foundation of config_036 and addresses a key design choice with minimal parameter changes.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and scvi_n200 RNA encoder (e.g., config_036) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests the impact of replacing the image encoder (imagenet_vit_l → resnet50) while keeping other components (scvi_n200 RNA, avgpool aggregation, concat fusion) consistent. This isolates the effect of image encoder choice, a critical design decision, and could clarify whether resnet50 offers better performance than imagenet_vit_l in this context.
